title: Fix visits RLS policies to cover alias and QR code visit rows
description:
## Bug
The visits RLS SELECT and INSERT policies only check url_object_id, but alias and QR code visits store NULL in that column — they only set alias_id or qr_code_id. This causes those visit rows to be invisible to users and INSERT to fail for anonymous redirect visitors hitting alias/QR routes.

## Root Cause
Both policies on the visits table use a single join path through url_object_id → url_objects.user_id = auth.uid(). When a visit is recorded via an alias or QR code, url_object_id is NULL, so the join produces no rows and RLS blocks access.

## Fix
New migration: drop and recreate both SELECT and INSERT policies on visits with three join paths:
1. url_object_id → url_objects.user_id = auth.uid() (existing)
2. alias_id → aliases.url_object_id → url_objects.user_id = auth.uid() (new)
3. qr_code_id → qr_codes.url_object_id → url_objects.user_id = auth.uid() (new)

INSERT policy: record_view is SECURITY DEFINER so anonymous users can call it — the INSERT policy needs to allow the postgres role or be permissive enough for the definer context.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] New migration file in supabase/migrations/
- [ ] SELECT policy covers url_object_id, alias_id, and qr_code_id join paths
- [ ] INSERT policy covers url_object_id, alias_id, and qr_code_id join paths
- [ ] pnpm lint passes
- [ ] pnpm test passes
- [ ] pnpm build passes
- [ ] Committed and pushed

title: Remove IPs from stored information
description:
We can't store IPs. We are a privacy focused company and our products echo that stance.

We need to swap out IPs for anonamized data. We are only going to use IPs in flight when determining location. We will store a hash (HMAC-265) of the IP instead of the value itself. That way we can (in the future) prevent abuse or do interesting collision detection.
design:
# IP Anonymization + Geolocation — Design Spec

**Issue:** qrky-kao  
**Date:** 2026-04-01  
**Status:** Approved

---

## Problem

QRky stores raw IP addresses in the `visits` table on every redirect and QR scan. As a privacy-focused product, raw IPs must not be persisted. The IP is only needed in-flight for geolocation purposes. What gets stored should be an anonymized hash that enables future abuse detection and collision analysis without revealing the original address.

---

## Goals

- Never persist a raw IP address
- Store an HMAC-SHA256 hash of the IP instead
- Resolve country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) and region (ISO 3166-2 subdivision) from the IP before discarding it
- Use MaxMind GeoLite2-City for geolocation
- Degrade gracefully when geo data is unavailable (store `"UNKNOWN"`)

---

## Out of Scope

- Automated GeoLite2 database updates (noted as future work — `.mmdb` file can be replaced on disk without a redeploy)
- Backfilling existing `visits` rows (existing data is test data; no migration needed)

---

## Data Flow

```
Request headers
    → enrichVisit(headers)
        → extract raw IP (x-forwarded-for || x-real-ip || "")
        → HMAC-SHA256(ip, HMAC_SECRET) → ipHash
        → GeoLite2 lookup(ip) → { country, region } || "UNKNOWN"
    → record_view RPC({ ip_hash, country, region, useragent, ... })
        → INSERT INTO visits
```

The raw IP never leaves `enrichVisit`. It is used in-flight only and immediately discarded.

---

## Database Changes

### Migration 1 — visits table schema

- Rename column `ip` → `ip_hash`
- Add column `country text` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g. `"ZA"`, or `"UNKNOWN"`)
- Add column `region text` (ISO 3166-2 subdivision code, e.g. `"ZA-WC"`, or `"UNKNOWN"`)

Existing rows are not backfilled. A comment in the migration records that pre-migration values in `ip_hash` are raw IPs from test data.

### Migration 2 — record_view function

Update the `record_view` Postgres function:

- Replace parameter `ip text` with `ip_hash text`
- Add parameters `country text` and `region text`
- Update the `INSERT INTO visits` statement to use the new column names and parameters

---

## Application Changes

### New file: `src/lib/enrich-visit.ts`

Responsibilities:
- Accept `ReadonlyHeaders`
- Extract raw IP from `x-forwarded-for` header (use the first IP if the header contains a comma-separated list), falling back to `x-real-ip`, then `""`
- Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the IP using Node's built-in `crypto` module (no new dependency) with the `HMAC_SECRET` env var as the key
- Look up country and region via `@maxmind/geoip2-node`, reading from the file at `GEOIP_DB_PATH`
- Return `{ ipHash: string, country: string, region: string }`

The GeoLite2 reader must be initialised once at module load as a singleton (not per-call) to avoid re-reading the `.mmdb` file on every request. If initialisation fails, the singleton is `null` and all lookups degrade to `"UNKNOWN"`.

Failure handling:
- If `GEOIP_DB_PATH` is not set, missing, or unreadable: `country` and `region` return `"UNKNOWN"`
- If the IP is not found in the database: `country` and `region` return `"UNKNOWN"`
- If the `.mmdb` file is corrupt or the reader throws: `country` and `region` return `"UNKNOWN"`
- Hashing always succeeds (empty string IP produces a valid hash)

### Updated: `src/lib/record-view.ts`

- Call `enrichVisit(headers)` to get `{ ipHash, country, region }`
- Pass `ip_hash`, `country`, `region` to the `record_view` RPC
- Remove direct IP extraction logic (now owned by `enrich-visit.ts`)

### New environment variables

| Variable | Description | Required |
|---|---|---|
| `HMAC_SECRET` | Secret key for HMAC-SHA256 IP hashing | Yes — hashing fails without it |
| `GEOIP_DB_PATH` | Absolute path to GeoLite2-City `.mmdb` file | Required for geo data; if missing, country/region degrade to `"UNKNOWN"` |

Both variables are server-side only and must never be exposed to the client. Both should be added to `.env.example` with placeholder values.

### New dependency

- `@maxmind/geoip2-node` — official MaxMind Node.js reader for `.mmdb` files

---

## Testing

### New: `src/lib/enrich-visit.test.ts`

- Hash output is deterministic for a given IP + secret
- Hash changes when the IP changes
- Hash changes when the secret changes
- Empty string IP produces a hash without error
- Returns correct country + region for a known IP (mocked GeoLite2 reader)
- Returns `"UNKNOWN"` for country and region when `GEOIP_DB_PATH` is not set
- Returns `"UNKNOWN"` when the IP is not found in the database
- Returns `"UNKNOWN"` when the `.mmdb` file is missing or corrupt

### Updated: `src/lib/record-view.test.ts`

- Mock `enrichVisit` and assert `record_view` RPC is called with `ip_hash`, `country`, `region` (not `ip`)
- Assert `enrichVisit` is called with the correct headers object
- Remove existing IP header extraction tests (that logic now lives in `enrich-visit.test.ts`)

---

## Deployment Notes

The GeoLite2-City `.mmdb` file is mounted as a volume in Coolify and referenced by `GEOIP_DB_PATH`. Updating the database requires only replacing the file on disk — no application redeploy needed.

Future work: automate updates via a cron job hitting the MaxMind download API.

title: WCAG 2.1 AA: Audit + fix all pages
description:
## Problem Statement
QRky operates in the EU. The European Accessibility Act requires WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. No a11y tooling or audit exists. Enforcement began June 2025.

## User Stories
- As a user with a screen reader or keyboard-only navigation, I want QRky to be fully accessible

## Constraints
- WCAG 2.1 AA (not 2.2 or AAA)
- vitest-axe and @axe-core/react as only new dev dependencies
- All existing tests must continue to pass

## Design
Full spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-13-gdpr-wcag-compliance-design.md Section 3

### Tooling
- src/components/dev/AxeProvider.tsx: Client Component, dynamic import of @axe-core/react in useEffect, dev-only
- Wrap {children} in src/app/layout.tsx with AxeProvider
- vitest.setup.ts: import vitest-axe/extend-expect, configureAxe({ runOnly: { type: 'tag', values: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa'] } })
- Each page test gains: const results = await axe(container); expect(results).toHaveNoViolations()

### Audit scope
All pages including:
- Auth: /login, /register, /login/forgot-password, /login/reset-password, /email-verification-waiting
- Dashboard: /dashboard/user, /dashboard/urls, /dashboard/urls/[uuid] and all sub-routes
- Public: /, /privacy, /terms
- Redirect: /u/[identifier], /q/[identifier], /qr/[uuid]
- New components: ConsentBanner, account deletion modal

### Known violations (from code inspection)
- dashboard/user/page.tsx: icon-only labels on inputs (no accessible text)
- layout.tsx: missing skip-to-main-content link
- DeleteButton.tsx: icon-only button with no aria-label
- Deletion modal: focus trap + return on close (spec'd in Section 1)
- ConsentBanner: role=region, aria-label, aria-live=polite (spec'd in Section 2)
- Page titles: verify all unique and descriptive
- Form errors: add aria-describedby linking inputs to error elements
- DaisyUI colours: check 4.5:1 contrast ratio; override failing tokens in tailwind.config.ts

Engineer must run full audit first and record ALL findings in docs/a11y-audit-2026-04-13.md before writing fixes.

## Success Metrics
- Zero axe violations across all pages
- vitest-axe prevents regression in CI
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] AxeProvider in src/components/dev/AxeProvider.tsx, wraps children in layout (dev-only dynamic import)
- [ ] vitest-axe in vitest.setup.ts with wcag2a + wcag2aa tags configured
- [ ] Each page test has toHaveNoViolations() assertion
- [ ] Audit findings in docs/a11y-audit-2026-04-13.md
- [ ] Zero axe violations across all audited pages
- [ ] Skip-to-main-content link in root layout with id=main-content on main wrapper
- [ ] All form inputs have programmatically associated labels
- [ ] All icon-only interactive elements have aria-label

- [ ] All page titles unique and descriptive
- [ ] Form errors associated via aria-describedby

title: GDPR: Analytics consent banner + policy versioning
description:
## Problem Statement
QRky loads Umami analytics unconditionally. Umami collects IP addresses + geo data (DISABLE_GEO_IP is off) = personal data under GDPR. EU law requires explicit consent before collection.

## User Stories
- As a visitor, I want to choose whether QRky collects analytics about my usage
- As a logged-in user, I want my consent preference to follow me across devices
- As a returning visitor, I want to be re-prompted when the privacy policy materially changes

## Constraints
- Self-hosted Umami only (no third-party trackers)
- Supabase Auth session cookies are strictly necessary — no consent needed for those
- No additional npm packages for consent logic (implement in-house)
- Only new dev deps: vitest-axe and @axe-core/react

## Design (full detail in spec doc)
Full spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-13-gdpr-wcag-compliance-design.md Section 2

Key points:
- POLICY_VERSION constant in src/lib/policy.ts (format: YYYY-MM-DD)
- Privacy + terms pages import POLICY_VERSION for last-updated date
- ConsentBanner Client Component (src/components/ui/consent/ConsentBanner.tsx)
  - Props: isAuthenticated, initialConsent (from Server Component), forceOpen + onClose (for footer link)
  - Fixed bottom bar, no dismiss without choice
  - Umami next/script injected only on acceptance
  - Internal state: consent, showBanner (initialised from prop, owned by component)
- DB migration: analytics_consent boolean, policy_version_consented text, analytics_consent_updated_at timestamptz on profiles
- Sync: DB takes precedence over localStorage on mount; prior localStorage consent propagated to DB for new logins
- updateAnalyticsConsent server action (src/app/actions/consent.ts) — DB write fail: log + silent fallback to localStorage
- Footer Cookie Preferences link: state lifted to root layout (showConsentPreferences boolean), passed as forceOpen to ConsentBanner
- Dashboard /dashboard/user: consent toggle showing status, version, timestamp
- Privacy policy Section 8 updated with Supabase cookie names and Umami disclosure

## ConsentBanner a11y
- role=region, aria-label=Cookie preferences
- aria-live=polite for screen reader announcement
- No focus trap (non-modal bar)
- Natural tab order through Accept/Decline buttons

## Out of Scope
- Full cookie consent management platform
- Granular consent per data category

## Success Metrics
- Umami script absent from DOM until consent accepted
- Existing users see banner on next visit (null consent columns)
- Policy version bump re-prompts all users
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] src/lib/policy.ts exports POLICY_VERSION
- [ ] Privacy and terms pages display POLICY_VERSION as last updated (not new Date())
- [ ] Unconditional Umami script removed from src/app/layout.tsx
- [ ] DB migration adds analytics_consent, policy_version_consented, analytics_consent_updated_at to profiles
- [ ] ConsentBanner shown when consent null or policy version mismatches
- [ ] Banner cannot be dismissed without choosing Accept or Decline
- [ ] Umami next/script only rendered after consent accepted
- [ ] Umami script absent from DOM when declined/null
- [ ] On mount with non-null DB consent: localStorage written to match
- [ ] On mount with null DB consent + localStorage set: updateAnalyticsConsent propagates to DB
- [ ] updateAnalyticsConsent DB write failure: silent fallback (no user error)
- [ ] Footer Cookie Preferences link re-opens banner via forceOpen prop
- [ ] Dashboard consent section shows status, version, timestamp, change button
- [ ] Privacy policy Section 8 updated with Supabase cookie names + Umami disclosure
- [ ] ConsentBanner has role=region, aria-label, aria-live=polite
- [ ] pnpm test && pnpm build pass

title: GDPR: Account deletion flow
description:
## Problem Statement
Users have no way to delete their account, violating GDPR Art. 17 (right to erasure).

## User Stories
- As a registered user, I want to permanently delete my account and all my data so I can exercise my GDPR right to erasure

## Constraints
- Hard delete only — no soft delete or anonymization
- All associated data must be destroyed: url_objects, aliases, qr_codes, visits (FK cascades already in place)
- Must show explicit warning that all links will break immediately

## Design
- 'Danger Zone' section at bottom of /dashboard/user
- Modal with type-DELETE confirmation (btn-error styling)
- Focus trapped in modal while open; returned to trigger on close
- Server action deleteAccount in src/app/dashboard/user/actions.ts
- Calls supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(userId) — cascades handle the rest
- signOut then redirect to /
- If deleteUser fails: surface error in modal, allow retry, no redirect
- If signOut fails after successful delete: redirect anyway (auth user is gone, session will be rejected)
- Defensive null check on user in action (middleware already protects route)
- Privacy policy Section 6 (src/app/privacy/page.tsx) updated with accurate deletion description and link

## Out of Scope
- Email confirmation loop
- Scheduled deletion / grace period

## Success Metrics
- User can self-serve delete account without contacting support
- All associated data gone from DB after deletion
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Danger Zone section visible at bottom of /dashboard/user
- [ ] Modal requires typing DELETE before submit enabled
- [ ] Modal traps focus when open; returns focus to trigger on close
- [ ] deleteAccount server action calls supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(userId)
- [ ] All data deleted via FK cascade (verified by unit test)
- [ ] User signed out and redirected to / after deletion
- [ ] Error displayed in modal on failure; retry possible
- [ ] Privacy policy Section 6 updated with link to /dashboard/user
- [ ] pnpm test && pnpm build pass

title: Spec review: Fix vitest-axe configuration example
description:

This only enables ONE rule (color-contrast). Spec says 'WCAG 2.1 AA ruleset explicitly configured' but example doesn't show how to enable full ruleset.

Provide correct configureAxe() call for full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.

title: Spec review: Fix state management pattern for consent banner sync
description:

Also: 'Cookie Preferences' footer link state lifting pattern not specified - which component holds the state to force banner re-render?

Specify state management architecture before planning.

title: Spec review: Fix error handling gaps in consent + deletion flows
description:
Missing error handling specs:
1. updateAnalyticsConsent server action - no error handling (DB write fail, should it fallback to localStorage? retry? user feedback?)
2. deleteAccount signOut failure - deletion succeeds but signOut fails, user deleted but has session cookie
3. deleteAccount defensive auth check - should action check user is non-null despite middleware?

Fix in spec before planning.
close_reason: Resolved in spec v3: deleteUser failure surfaces error in modal with retry; signOut failure after successful delete redirects anyway (session rejected since auth user gone); defensive null check specified in action.

vi.clearAllMocks();

vi.restoreAllMocks();

title: Subscription Tiers - free/paid model with Stripe integration
description:
## Problem Statement
QRky has no monetization strategy. Users can create unlimited URLs, QR codes, and aliases for free, which limits revenue potential and does not differentiate casual users from power users.

## Spec Reference
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-19-subscription-tiers-design.md

## User Stories
- As a casual user, I want to try QRky for free with basic URL shortening so I can evaluate the product before paying
- As a small business owner, I want affordable access to QR codes and custom aliases so I can brand my links professionally
- As a marketing agency, I want higher volume limits with predictable pricing so I can manage multiple client campaigns
- As an enterprise customer, I want unlimited usage with custom terms so I can scale without constraints

## Subscription Tiers
- Free: 5 URLs, no QR codes, no aliases, analytics up to 1M clicks
- Basic (10 EUR/month): 100 URLs/QRs/aliases, 14-day free trial
- Pro (25 EUR/month): 500 URLs/QRs/aliases, 14-day free trial
- Enterprise: unlimited, contact sales

## Annual billing: configurable discount (default 17% = 2 months free)

## 1:1:1 Bundle Rule
Every paid tier: each URL includes 1 QR code and 1 alias. Hard limits enforced at creation time.

## Key Constraints
- No QR code or alias creation on free tier (UI disabled with tooltip)
- Hard limit enforcement with upgrade modal when limits reached
- Real-time usage counter in dashboard, warning at 80% capacity
- 14-day trial: no credit card required, once per user, auto-downgrades to free if no payment
- Enterprise: manual admin assignment, no self-service

## Dependencies
- Stripe for payment processing
- Supabase Auth (existing)
- Database schema updates for tier tracking (user tier, trial status, trial end date)
- Email service for trial reminder emails

## Out of Scope
- Team/organization accounts
- Multiple payment methods
- Usage-based billing / overages
- Custom domains
- API rate limiting by tier
- White-label / affiliate program

# What are we doing?
Create a GitHub Actions CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs the QRky test suite on every push and pull request.

Steps:
1. Create .github/workflows/ci.yml
2. Trigger on: push (all branches) and pull_request (targeting main)
3. Use ubuntu-latest runner with Node.js (match version in .nvmrc or package.json engines)
4. Install pnpm via corepack or setup-pnpm action

There is currently no automated CI pipeline. Tests and builds are only run locally before push. A GitHub Actions workflow ensures every PR is validated automatically, catching regressions before merge.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml exists and is valid YAML

title: CI: Add push trigger to workflow
description:
The CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml only triggers on pull_request. It should also trigger on push to all branches so that direct pushes to feature branches are validated, not just PRs.

Change the trigger from:
  on:
    pull_request:
      branches: ["*"]

To:
  on:
    push:
    pull_request:
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Workflow triggers on both push and pull_request
- [ ] CI runs on direct branch pushes (not just PRs)

title: CI: Add pnpm build step to workflow
description:
The CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml runs lint and test but is missing the pnpm build step. Build catches Server/Client serialization errors and prerender issues that unit tests miss — it is a required quality gate per AGENTS.md.

Add a Build step after Test:
  - name: Build
    run: pnpm build
    env:
      NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL }}
      NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY }}

Placeholder values are sufficient if real secrets are not configured (build only needs these to be non-empty strings).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] pnpm build step present in .github/workflows/ci.yml
- [ ] Build runs after test in CI
- [ ] Env vars passed to build step
- [ ] Workflow passes end-to-end on a PR

title: Add meaningful content assertions to alias/new page tests (replace toBeDefined smoke tests)
description:
## Problem
src/app/dashboard/urls/[uuid]/alias/new/page.test.tsx has two tests that assert only expect(result).toBeDefined(). Comments in the test explain they guard against serialization errors, which is a valid concern — but the tests provide no assertion about rendered content.

## What to do
Without removing the serialization regression protection, add assertions that verify:
1. The page renders an input field for the alias
2. The page renders a submit button
3. URL data (fetched by the page) appears in the rendered output

This makes the tests meaningful while keeping the serialization protection.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] At least 2 content assertions added (input field, submit button, or URL data)
- [ ] Existing serialization regression guard is preserved
- [ ] pnpm test passes
close_reason: Implemented and tests passing - added meaningful content assertions for alias form, uuid, and URL data while preserving serialization regression guard

title: Add unit tests for QRkySVG rendering engine
description:
## Problem
QRkySVG is the most complex custom code in the project and has zero tests. Key methods like getRoundedSquarePath, determineModuleShape, getLogo, getModuleValue, and header are completely untested.

## What to do
Add a test file (or expand qr-code.test.ts) for QRkySVG covering:
1. Generated SVG contains expected <svg> root element
2. Custom foreground/background colors appear in SVG output
3. getLogo returns null when no logo set, SVG string when logo set
4. Module shape variations (round vs square) produce different path data
5. header() produces valid SVG header string

This is P3 as the QR generation is tested end-to-end via generateQrCode, but unit coverage of the rendering internals is missing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] At least 5 test cases covering QRkySVG methods
- [ ] Color customisation verified in SVG output (not just contains('<svg'))
- [ ] getLogo tested for null and populated cases
- [ ] pnpm test passes
close_reason: Implemented and tests passing - added 10 tests covering SVG generation, custom colors, viewBox sizes, logo handling, module shapes, and various input strings
